 ORDER
Heard with the aid of case diary

This is repeat second bail application filed under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. for grant of bail to the applicant, in connection with FIR/Crime No.520/2022, Date:-(Not mentioned) registered at P.S.-Jawad, District- Neemuch (M.P.) for commission of offence punishable under Sections 363,
366, 376 (2)(N), 376(3) of the IPC and sections 5/6 of the POCSO Act.
2.
Prosecution story, in brief is that, at the time of the incident the prosecutrix was around 15 years 4 months of age.
The prosecutrix and the applicant knew each other before the incident.
On 14/11/2022 the prosecutrix called the applicant, thereafter both of them met in village Nayagaon and went to Gujarat by public transport.

The applicant and the prosecutrix solemnized their Pintu vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 15 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/90470509/
1 marriage in a temple by exchanging flower garland and started to live as husband and wife.

sentences.text: Both of them lived together for 5 months and 20 days in Gujarat and Maharashtra.
Meanwhile the applicant committed sexual intercourse with her after obtaining her consent.
On 04/05/2023 the police had recovered the prosecutrix from possession of the applicant.
3. Learned counsel for the applicant/ accused submits that, the applicant has not committed the offence and has falsely been implicated in the case.
The applicant had not taken the prosecutrix anywhere forcibly.
The prosecutrix herself had called the applicant and voluntarily went with him.
There was love and affection between them.
Case of prosecution is not supported by MLC and DNA report.
The case was fixed firstly for the prosecution evidence on 17/07/2023, but neither prosecutrix not other witnesses have been examined till now.

While as provided u/s 35(1) of the POCSO Act, 2012, the statement of the prosecutrix shall be recorded within 30 days from taking cognizance for the offence by the special court and as provided u/s 35(2), the special court shall complete the trial, as far as possible within a period of 1 year from the date of taking cognizance of the offence.
It is also submitted that the special court has taken cognizance for the offence on 21/06/2023.
Thereafter, more than 5 months have elapsed, but still the statement of prosecutrix has not been recorded.
The applicant is in custody since 05/05/2023.
Trial will take considerable long time for its disposal, therefore, it is prayed that the applicant be released on bail.
4. On other hand learned counsel for the non-applicant/State has opposed the prayer and submits that at the time of the incident, the prosecutrix was below 16 years of age.
Therefore, her consent is immaterial.
The offence is serious in nature.
Hence, the applicant is not entitled for bail.

5. Having heard learned counsel for the parties, perused the case-diary also considering the age of prosecutrix and circumstances of the case, in view of this court, it is not a fit case to grant bail to the applicant.
Resultantly, application for bail is rejected.
(PRAKASH CHANDRA GUPTA) JUDGE ajit Pintu vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 15 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/90470509/
